key_insight: Gate3DGen selectively cleans up real-world images before single-image 3D generation, while leaving clean inputs unchanged. It works with existing 3D generators without retraining them.
problem_solved: 3D generators that perform well on curated images can struggle with uneven lighting, blur, and occlusions. Pre-processing must address these defects without removing visual cues needed to reconstruct 3D objects.
method: Use a degradation-aware router to decide whether an input needs purification.
Selectively purify degraded images while preserving cues important for 3D generation; bypass clean inputs.
Pass the resulting image to an existing 3D generator without retraining that generator.
impact: This approach aims to make existing 3D generation pipelines more useful for everyday photos without costly generator retraining. The supplied abstract is truncated and provides no quantitative results.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input image → degradation-aware router → bypass or purification → 3D generator.
Degradation icons illustrating uneven illumination, blur, and occlusion.
Split-path illustration showing clean images passed through unchanged and degraded images selectively processed.
Object-cue diagram highlighting the visual information purification must preserve for 3D reconstruction.
paper_title: Gate3DGen: A Pre-processing Model that Selectively Purifies Real-World Images for 3D Generation
paper_authors: Xiaolin Li, Zihao Huang, Fanpeng Meng, Chen Yang, Guanjun Wu
